tldr: Wealthsimple is the most direct competitor mover today, with a CAD stablecoin beta, a 3.25% promo on its CADD beta and new kids and teens accounts. Elsewhere, stablecoins and tokenized deposits are moving into mainstream banking, and AI agents and voice are reshaping app interactions.
themes: Stablecoins and tokenized deposits going mainstream
AI agents and voice in banking apps
Payroll and direct deposit as a primary-account wedge

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple opened a retail beta for Tetra's Canadian-dollar stablecoin and a CADD beta with 3.25% promotional rewards.
highlights.why: The closest Canadian rival is putting a CAD-denominated digital dollar and a rewards promo in front of retail users. Simplii should decide its position on stablecoin and digital-cash features and on competing with the 3.25% promo.

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple launched kids and teens accounts.
highlights.why: This is a direct play for the next generation of customers and household relationships. Simplii should check its youth and family offering and its long-term acquisition funnel.

highlights.headline: SoFi took its bank-issued stablecoin SoFiUSD live on Polygon, billed as the first tokenized deposit product at a US bank.
highlights.why: A regulated bank is offering tokenized deposits to a base of 17M members, which sets a precedent for what customers may expect from a digital bank. Simplii should watch for Canadian regulatory and competitor follow-through.

highlights.headline: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet so AI agents can pay on users' behalf without seeing card details, and Starling launched an AI 'talk to transact' payments feature.
highlights.why: Agent-initiated and conversational payments are becoming a new expectation. Simplii should consider how its cards, payments and app experience would work with agents and voice.
